items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
items.exp: keep+목적어+형용사 구조에서 목적격 보어 자리에는 부사가 올 수 없어요. ③ safely는 형용사 safe가 되어야 해요. ⑤의 let 뒤 동사원형 enjoy는 올바르고, ① for 뒤 동명사도 맞아요.
items.passage: National parks are special places [① for preserving] nature. They [② keep] many animal and plant species [③ safely]. At the same time, they [④ let] people [⑤ enjoy] the beauty of nature.

items.q:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
Let's take a short break, ___?
items.exp: Let's ~로 시작하는 제안문의 부가의문문은 shall we?를 써요. will we, don't we 등은 Let's 문장에 쓰지 않아요.
items.passage: Let's take a look at two famous national parks in South America and Africa.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 preserving과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
items.exp: preserve는 '보존하다, 보호하다'라는 뜻이라 protect와 의미가 가까워요. destroy는 반의어예요.
items.passage: National parks are special places for [preserving] nature.

items.q:
윗글의 They keep many animal and plant species safe.와 같은 구조를 사용해 다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
그 코트는 너를 따뜻하게 유지해 준다.
choices: The coat keeps to you warm.
The coat keeps you to warm.
items.exp: 「keep+목적어+형용사」 어순이어서 keeps you warm이 맞아요. 보어 자리에는 부사(warmly)나 to부정사를 쓰지 않고, 목적어가 형용사보다 앞에 와요.
items.passage: They [keep] many animal and plant species safe.

items.q: 윗글 바로 다음에 이어질 내용으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 남아메리카와 아프리카에 있는 유명한 국립공원 두 곳의 소개
국립공원에서 지켜야 할 안전 수칙 목록
동식물 종의 멸종 원인에 대한 통계 자료
한국 국립공원의 입장료와 운영 시간 안내
items.exp: 마지막 문장 Let's take a look at two famous national parks in South America and Africa.가 다음에 소개할 내용을 알려 줘요. 나머지는 글에서 예고한 내용이 아니에요.
items.passage: National parks are special places for preserving nature. They keep many animal and plant species safe. At the same time, they let people enjoy the beauty of nature. Let's take a look at two famous national parks in South America and Africa.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 국립공원은 사람들이 자연의 아름다움을 즐기게 해 준다.
글쓴이는 유럽과 아시아의 국립공원 세 곳을 살펴보자고 한다.
글쓴이는 남미와 아프리카의 국립공원 두 곳을 살펴보자고 한다.
국립공원은 자연을 보존하기 위한 특별한 장소이다.
국립공원은 많은 동식물 종을 안전하게 지킨다.
items.exp: 마지막 문장에서 살펴볼 곳은 남미와 아프리카의 유명한 국립공원 '두 곳'이에요. 유럽·아시아 세 곳이라는 보기만 본문과 달라요.
items.passage: National parks are special places for preserving nature. They keep many animal and plant species safe. At the same time, they let people enjoy the beauty of nature. Let's take a look at two famous national parks in South America and Africa.

items.q: 윗글의 첫 문장처럼 Can you believe 뒤에 절이 이어질 때, 어법상 올바른 문장은?
choices: Can you believe that is he only ten years old?
Can you believe him is only ten years old?
Can you believe he to be only ten years old?
Can you believe he is only ten years old?
Can you believe is he only ten years old?
items.exp: believe 뒤에는 접속사 that(생략 가능)과 「주어+동사」 어순의 절이 와요. 의문문 어순으로 도치하거나 목적격·to부정사를 쓰면 틀려요.
items.passage: [Can you believe you can experience four seasons in one day?]

items.q:
빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
Busan is famous (A) its seafood. Einstein is famous (B) a scientist.
items.exp: be famous for는 '~로 유명하다(이유)', be famous as는 '~로서 유명하다(자격)'예요. 해산물은 유명한 이유라 for, 과학자는 자격이라 as를 써요.
items.passage: It is [famous for] its dynamic weather.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 single과 의미가 같은 것은?
choices: My uncle is still [single] at forty.
Not a [single] student was late for class today.
He stayed [single] for his whole life.
She is a [single] mother of two kids.
items.exp: 본문의 single은 '단 하나의'라는 뜻이고, 첫 번째 문장의 single도 '단 한 명의'예요. 나머지 보기는 모두 '독신의, 혼자인'을 뜻해요.
items.passage: It can be sunny, rainy, or snowy in a [single] day!

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 even과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: The road is not [even], so drive slowly.
[Even] a little child can solve this puzzle.
He spoke in a calm and [even] voice.
This book is [even] more interesting than that one.
items.exp: 본문의 even은 '심지어 ~조차'라는 뜻의 부사예요. 첫 번째 보기가 같은 뜻이에요. 비교급 앞 even은 '훨씬', 나머지는 '동점의, 평평한, 한결같은' 뜻의 형용사예요.
items.passage: Also, you can see mountains, lakes, and [even] a big ice field in this park.

items.q:
윗글을 참고하여 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
The lake, one of the deepest lakes in the world, ___ many tourists.
items.exp: 콤마 사이의 one of ~는 앞 명사를 설명하는 동격 표현이라 문장의 주어는 The lake(단수)예요. 따라서 단수 동사 attracts가 맞아요.
items.passage: For example, Grey Glacier, one of the most wonderful glaciers in Chile, welcomes you in the park.

items.q:
빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
It is important (A) us to save water. It is kind (B) you to help me.
items.exp: 가주어-진주어 구문에서 to부정사의 의미상 주어는 보통 for+목적격이에요. 다만 kind처럼 사람의 성격을 나타내는 형용사 뒤에서는 of+목적격을 써요.
items.passage: It is exciting to walk on the glacier and enjoy the icy view.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 방문객은 하루 동안 한 가지 날씨만 경험하게 된다.
이 공원에서는 산, 호수, 큰 빙원을 볼 수 있다.
그레이 빙하는 칠레에서 가장 멋진 빙하 중 하나로 소개된다.
빙하 위를 걷고 경치를 즐기는 것은 흥미진진하다고 한다.
items.exp: 맑음·비·눈이 단 하루 안에 모두 나타날 수 있다고 했으니 한 가지 날씨만 경험한다는 말은 틀려요.
items.passage: Can you believe you can experience four seasons in one day? Torres del Paine National Park in Chile is the perfect place for this. It is famous for its dynamic weather. It can be sunny, rainy, or snowy in a single day! Also, you can see mountains, lakes, and even a big ice field in this park. For example, Grey Glacier, one of the most wonderful glaciers in Chile, welcomes you in the park. It is exciting to walk on the glacier and enjoy the icy view.

items.q:
윗글을 읽고 다음 질문에 답한 것으로 알맞은 것은?
Why is Torres del Paine National Park the perfect place to experience four seasons in one day?
choices: Because its weather is so dynamic that it can change in a single day.
Because it is covered with ice all year round.
Because visitors can stay there for four seasons.
Because it has four different parks in one area.
Because the glaciers move from season to season.
items.exp: 이 공원은 역동적인 날씨로 유명해서 하루 안에 맑고, 비 오고, 눈이 올 수 있어요. 나머지 보기는 본문에 없는 내용이에요.
items.passage: Can you believe you can experience four seasons in one day? Torres del Paine National Park in Chile is the perfect place for this. It is famous for its dynamic weather. It can be sunny, rainy, or snowy in a single day! Also, you can see mountains, lakes, and even a big ice field in this park. For example, Grey Glacier, one of the most wonderful glaciers in Chile, welcomes you in the park. It is exciting to walk on the glacier and enjoy the icy view.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
items.exp: 전치사 for 뒤에는 명사나 동명사가 와야 해요. ④ for hike는 for hiking이 되어야 해요. ⑤ makes visitors take는 사역동사 뒤 동사원형이라 맞아요.
items.passage: The park [① is making] efforts [② to preserve] its natural beauty. Second, only some park trails [③ are] open to visitors [④ for hike]. Third, the park makes visitors [⑤ take] their trash with them when they leave.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 to preserve를 바꿔 쓸 때 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사는 in order to(또는 so as to)로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. to가 빠지거나 because of를 쓰면 틀려요.
items.passage: The park is making efforts [to preserve] its natural beauty.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 open과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: She will [open] a new cafe next year.
I want to [open] a bank account.
The museum is [open] to everyone on Sundays.
items.exp: 본문의 open은 be동사 뒤에서 '개방된'을 뜻하는 형용사예요. 첫 번째 보기도 형용사이고, 나머지는 '열다'를 뜻하는 동사예요.
items.passage: Second, only some park trails are [open] to visitors for hiking.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: Dad made me to wash the car.
Mr. Kim let us go home early.
My mom had me clean my room.
The coach got the players to run faster.
She helped me finish my homework.
items.exp: make는 사역동사라 「make+목적어+동사원형」을 써서 made me wash가 되어야 해요. get은 to부정사, help는 원형·to부정사 모두 가능해요.
items.passage: Third, the park [makes] visitors take their trash with them when they leave.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 올바른 문장은?
choices: There are one more rule for visitors.
There is two more rules for visitors.
There is many visitors in the park.
There are a lot of trash on the beach.
There is a lot of trash on the beach.
items.exp: There is/are 뒤 명사의 수에 be동사를 맞춰요. trash는 셀 수 없는 명사라 is가 맞아요. 복수 명사(rules, visitors)에는 are를, 단수 one more rule에는 is를 써요.
items.passage: [There's] one more thing: the hotels in the park do not use plastic and only use eco-friendly products.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 공원 안 호텔은 플라스틱을 쓰지 않는다.
방문객 수를 통제하기 때문에 방문객은 예약해야 한다.
방문객은 떠날 때 자신의 쓰레기를 가져가야 한다.
방문객은 입장료만 내면 예약 없이 들어갈 수 있다.
items.exp: 입장하려면 예약(book)을 해야 한다고 했어요. 입장료만 내면 예약이 필요 없다는 말은 본문과 달라요.
items.passage: The park is making efforts to preserve its natural beauty. First, it controls the number of visitors, so they should book to enter the park. Second, only some park trails are open to visitors for hiking. Third, the park makes visitors take their trash with them when they leave. There's one more thing: the hotels in the park do not use plastic and only use eco-friendly products.

items.q:
윗글을 읽고 다음 질문에 답한 것으로 알맞은 것은?
Why should visitors book before entering Torres del Paine National Park?
choices: Because the trails are closed in summer.
Because the park controls the number of visitors.
Because the hotels are always full.
Because it is the first national park in the world.
Because visitors must take their trash home.
items.exp: 공원이 방문객 수를 통제하기 때문에(so) 방문객이 예약해야 해요. 나머지는 예약해야 하는 이유로 본문에 나오지 않아요.
items.passage: The park is making efforts to preserve its natural beauty. First, it controls the number of visitors, so they should book to enter the park. Second, only some park trails are open to visitors for hiking. Third, the park makes visitors take their trash with them when they leave. There's one more thing: the hotels in the park do not use plastic and only use eco-friendly products.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: The baby slept peaceful in the car.
The lions walk slowly across the road.
Rhinos can move around freely in the park.
He ran quickly to the gate.
She spoke softly to the baby.
items.exp: 동사를 꾸미는 말은 부사여야 해요. slept를 꾸미려면 peaceful이 아니라 peacefully를 써야 해요. 나머지는 모두 부사가 동사를 꾸며요.
items.passage: Many wild animals move around this park [freely].

items.q: 윗글의 rhinos which are sleeping under baobab trees에서 「관계대명사+be동사」를 생략한 형태로 알맞은 것은?
choices: rhinos are sleeping under baobab trees
rhinos which sleeping under baobab trees
rhinos what are sleeping under baobab trees
rhinos whom are sleeping under baobab trees
items.exp: 「주격 관계대명사+be동사」는 함께 생략할 수 있어서 sleeping이 rhinos를 바로 꾸며요. which만 남기거나 whom, what을 쓰면 틀리고, are sleeping만 쓰면 절이 되어 버려요.
items.passage: If you are lucky, you can see rhinos [which are sleeping] under baobab trees.

items.q: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: 앞에서는 빅 파이브를 자유롭게 볼 수 있다는 긍정적 내용이고, 뒤에서는 위험에 처해 있다는 반대 내용이에요. 그래서 대조의 However가 알맞아요.
items.passage: Many wild animals move around this park freely. If you are lucky, you can see rhinos which are sleeping under baobab trees. ( ), the Big Five are in danger because of too much hunting.

items.q:
윗글의 To protect처럼 목적을 나타내는 to부정사를 사용하여 다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
강을 깨끗하게 유지하기 위해 우리는 매주 쓰레기를 줍는다.
choices: To keep the river cleanly, we pick up trash every week.
To keep the river clean, we picking up trash every week.
For keep the river clean, we pick up trash every week.
To keep the river clean, we pick up trash every week.
To keeping the river clean, we pick up trash every week.
items.exp: 목적은 「To+동사원형」으로 나타내고, keep+목적어+형용사 구조라 보어는 clean이어야 해요. 또 문장의 동사는 pick up으로 써야 해요.
items.passage: [To protect] the Big Five, the park has been a "no-hunting" area from the start.

items.q:
빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
Where is Tom? He has (A) to the library, so he isn't here.
Have you ever (B) to Jeju?
items.exp: has gone to는 '~로 가고 없다(결과)', have been to는 '~에 가 본 적 있다(경험)'를 뜻해요. Tom이 지금 여기 없으므로 (A)는 gone, 경험을 묻는 (B)는 been이에요.
items.passage: To protect the Big Five, the park [has been] a "no-hunting" area from the start.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 are used to와 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: He [used to] play soccer after school.
We got [used to] the cold weather.
My sister is [used to] waking up early.
Salt is [used to] make food taste better.
items.exp: 본문의 「be used to+동사원형」은 '~하는 데 사용되다'(수동태)예요. 첫 번째 보기가 같아요. be used to+-ing는 '익숙하다', used to+동사원형은 '~하곤 했다'예요.
items.passage: These days, drones and helicopters [are used to] monitor hunting activities.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 바오밥 나무 아래에서 자고 있는 코뿔소를 볼 수도 있다.
빅 파이브는 오염 때문에 위험에 처해 있다.
빅 파이브에는 치타와 기린이 들어 있다.
items.exp: 운이 좋으면 바오밥 나무 아래에서 자는 코뿔소를 볼 수 있다고 했어요. 나머지는 빅 파이브 구성, 위치(남아프리카), 위험 원인(사냥), 금지 대상(사냥)이 모두 달라요.
items.passage: Have you heard about the Big Five? They are lions, leopards, elephants, rhinos, and buffaloes. You can see them all in Kruger National Park in South Africa. Many wild animals move around this park freely. If you are lucky, you can see rhinos which are sleeping under baobab trees. However, the Big Five are in danger because of too much hunting. To protect the Big Five, the park has been a "no-hunting" area from the start. These days, drones and helicopters are used to monitor hunting activities.

items.q:
윗글을 읽고 다음 질문에 답한 것으로 알맞은 것은?
What are drones and helicopters used for in Kruger National Park?
choices: They are used to hunt rhinos from the sky.
They are used to monitor hunting activities.
They are used to bring food to the animals.
They are used to carry visitors across the park.
They are used to build camps for volunteers.
items.exp: 마지막 문장에서 드론과 헬리콥터는 사냥 활동을 감시하는 데 사용된다고 했어요.
items.passage: Have you heard about the Big Five? They are lions, leopards, elephants, rhinos, and buffaloes. You can see them all in Kruger National Park in South Africa. Many wild animals move around this park freely. If you are lucky, you can see rhinos which are sleeping under baobab trees. However, the Big Five are in danger because of too much hunting. To protect the Big Five, the park has been a "no-hunting" area from the start. These days, drones and helicopters are used to monitor hunting activities.

items.q:
윗글의 내용을 요약한 문장의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
The Big Five are in (A) because of too much hunting, so Kruger National Park has been a (B) area from the start.
items.exp: 과도한 사냥 때문에 빅 파이브가 위험(danger)에 처했고, 이를 막기 위해 처음부터 사냥 금지(no-hunting) 지역이었어요.
items.passage: Have you heard about the Big Five? They are lions, leopards, elephants, rhinos, and buffaloes. You can see them all in Kruger National Park in South Africa. Many wild animals move around this park freely. If you are lucky, you can see rhinos which are sleeping under baobab trees. However, the Big Five are in danger because of too much hunting. To protect the Big Five, the park has been a "no-hunting" area from the start. These days, drones and helicopters are used to monitor hunting activities.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
items.exp: 두 동사 monitor와 remove는 and로 연결된 병렬 구조이고 주어 Volunteers가 복수라 둘 다 복수형이어야 해요. ④ removes는 remove가 되어야 해요.
items.passage: Also, the park runs [① many] nature volunteer programs. Volunteers [② monitor] signs of [③ illegal] hunting activities and [④ removes] animal traps. National parks preserve [⑤ the Earth's] past, present, and future.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 signs와 의미가 같은 것은?
choices: Dark clouds are a [sign] of rain.
She put up a [sign] at the shop door.
items.exp: 본문의 signs of illegal hunting은 '징후'예요. 첫 번째 보기의 a sign of rain도 '징후'를 뜻하고, 나머지는 '표지판' 또는 '서명하다'예요.
items.passage: Volunteers monitor [signs] of illegal hunting activities and remove animal traps.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 Thanks to them과 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것은?
items.exp: thanks to는 '~ 덕분에'라는 뜻으로 because of와 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. because와 although 뒤에는 절이 와야 하고, in spite of와 instead of는 뜻이 달라요.
items.passage: [Thanks to them], future generations will also be able to experience many natural wonders.

items.q:
윗글의 주어를 A volunteer로 바꿀 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
A volunteer (A) signs of illegal hunting activities and (B) animal traps.
items.exp: 주어가 단수(A volunteer)이고 현재 시제이므로 두 동사 모두 -s가 붙어요. and로 연결된 두 동사는 형태를 같게 맞춰야 해요.
items.passage: Volunteers monitor signs of illegal hunting activities and remove animal traps.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: My brother will can drive next year.
I was able to find the trail.
She will be able to speak English well.
Are you able to see the lions?
They won't be able to enter without a reservation.
items.exp: can은 will과 함께 쓸 수 없어서 will be able to로 바꿔야 해요. 나머지는 모두 be able to를 올바르게 썼어요.
items.passage: Thanks to them, future generations will also [be able to] experience many natural wonders.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 현재 세대만 자연의 경이로움을 경험할 수 있다.
items.exp: 자원봉사자들은 불법 사냥 활동의 징후를 관찰하고 덫을 제거해요. 덫을 만든다, 교육 프로그램, 미래만 보존한다, 현재 세대만 경험한다는 말은 모두 틀려요.
items.passage: Also, the park runs many nature volunteer programs. Volunteers monitor signs of illegal hunting activities and remove animal traps. National parks preserve the Earth's past, present, and future. Thanks to them, future generations will also be able to experience many natural wonders.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 두 It에 대한 설명으로 옳은 것은?
choices: 첫 번째 It은 the river를 가리키고, 두 번째 It은 가주어이다.
첫 번째 It은 비인칭 주어이고, 두 번째 It은 the environment를 가리킨다.
두 It 모두 The park를 가리킨다.
첫 번째 It은 가주어이고, 두 번째 It은 The park를 가리킨다.
items.exp: 첫 번째 It is also possible to swim ~의 It은 to swim ~을 대신하는 가주어이고, 두 번째 It monitors the environment의 It은 앞 문장의 The park예요.
items.passage: [It] is also possible to swim in the river. The park is working hard to protect nature. [It] monitors the environment and makes visitors take their trash with them when they leave.

items.q:
윗글의 내용을 요약한 문장의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
Visitors can (A) boats to explore the islands, and the park makes them take their (B) with them when they leave.
items.exp: 방문객은 배를 타고(ride) 섬을 탐험하고, 떠날 때 쓰레기(trash)를 가져가야 해요.
items.passage: Thousand Islands National Park is a beautiful place on the St. Lawrence River. The park is famous for its many small islands and fun activities. Visitors can ride boats to explore the islands and enjoy many hiking trails. It is also possible to swim in the river. The park is working hard to protect nature. It monitors the environment and makes visitors take their trash with them when they leave.

items.q: Which is NOT true about Thousand Islands National Park?
choices: Visitors can ride boats to explore the islands.
It is famous for its many small islands.
The park is famous for its high mountains and deserts.
It is on the St. Lawrence River.
The park makes visitors take their trash with them.
items.exp: 공원은 높은 산과 사막이 아니라 많은 작은 섬과 즐거운 활동으로 유명해요.
items.passage: Thousand Islands National Park is a beautiful place on the St. Lawrence River. The park is famous for its many small islands and fun activities. Visitors can ride boats to explore the islands and enjoy many hiking trails. It is also possible to swim in the river. The park is working hard to protect nature. It monitors the environment and makes visitors take their trash with them when they leave.

items.q:
위 보고서와 같은 형식으로 다른 국립공원의 정보를 정리하려고 한다. 다음 문장이 들어갈 항목은?
"Sunflowers and pine trees grow in the park."
items.exp: 해바라기와 소나무는 식물이라서 Plants 항목에 들어가요. 보고서에서도 roses and asters가 Plants에 쓰였어요.
items.passage:
Yellowstone National Park
Location: Wyoming, the U.S.
Animals: black bears, mountain goats, and mountain lions
Plants: roses and asters
Weather: It is easy to see thunderstorms in the summer.
Features: (1) It is the first national park in the world. (2) Yellowstone Lake is in the park.

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 문장과 의미가 같은 것은?
choices: We can easily see thunderstorms in the summer.
Thunderstorms are hard to see in the summer.
It is easy to see thunderstorms in the winter.
It is difficult to see thunderstorms in the summer.
We rarely see thunderstorms in the summer.
items.exp: It is easy to see ~는 '~을 보기 쉽다'이므로 '쉽게 볼 수 있다'와 같아요. 나머지는 계절이 바뀌거나 '어렵다, 드물다'는 반대 의미예요.
items.passage:
Yellowstone National Park
Location: Wyoming, the U.S.
Animals: black bears, mountain goats, and mountain lions
Plants: roses and asters
Weather: [It is easy to see thunderstorms in the summer.]
Features: (1) It is the first national park in the world. (2) Yellowstone Lake is in the park.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
그것은 한국에서 가장 오래된 국립공원이다.
choices: It is the most old national park in Korea.
It is oldest national park in Korea.
It is the oldest national park in Korea.
It is the oldest national parks in Korea.
It is the oldest national park in the Korea.
items.exp: old의 최상급은 the oldest이고 뒤에는 단수 명사가 와요. the 없이 쓰거나 most old, 복수 명사, 고유명사 앞 the는 모두 틀려요.
items.passage: (1) It is the first national park in the world.

items.q: 다음 중 질문과 대답이 어법상 자연스럽게 이어지는 것은?
choices: Why pandas are in danger? - Because people have destroyed their habitat.
Why are pandas in danger? - Because people have destroyed their habitat.
Why are pandas in danger? - Because they hunted by people too often.
Why are pandas in danger? - Because of people have destroyed their habitat.
Why do pandas in danger? - Because people have destroyed their habitat.
items.exp: 의문사 의문문은 「Why+be동사+주어 ~?」 어순이에요. because 뒤에는 절이 오고(because of는 명사), 수동태는 are hunted처럼 be동사가 필요해요.
items.passage:
Lions
Food: large animals
Home: Africa
Size: 1.3-2.5 m
Why are they in danger? They are in danger because they are hunted by people too often.
"It is important to save lions!"

items.q: 윗글의 카드에 들어 있지 않은 항목은?
items.exp: 카드에는 먹이(Food), 서식지(Home), 크기(Size), 위험에 처한 이유가 나와 있고 몸무게(Weight)는 없어요.
items.passage:
Lions
Food: large animals
Home: Africa
Size: 1.3-2.5 m
Why are they in danger? They are in danger because they are hunted by people too often.
"It is important to save lions!"

items.q: 윗글의 밑줄 친 After와 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: [After] she finished lunch, she went to the library.
items.exp: 본문의 After는 뒤에 「주어+동사」(I learned)가 이어지는 접속사예요. 첫 번째 보기도 절(she finished)이 이어져요. 나머지는 명사가 이어지는 전치사예요.
items.passage: I use a wooden toothbrush. [After] I learned that plastic is not good for the environment, I decided to change my toothbrush.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 올바른 문장은?
choices: I finished to change my toothbrush.
I gave up to change my toothbrush.
I enjoy to change my toothbrush.
I mind to change my toothbrush.
I decided to change my toothbrush.
items.exp: decide는 to부정사를 목적어로 취해요. enjoy, finish, mind, give up은 동명사(-ing)를 목적어로 취해서 나머지는 모두 틀려요.
items.passage: I decided [to change] my toothbrush.

items.q:
-ful을 붙여 형용사를 만든다는 것을 바탕으로 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
Please be (A) with the glass cups. Thank you for your (B) advice.
items.exp: be동사 뒤 보어 자리와 명사 advice 앞에는 형용사가 와야 해요. care+ful=careful, help+ful=helpful이에요.
items.passage:
beauty + -ful → beautiful
wonder + -ful → wonderful
hope + -ful → hopeful

items.q:
괄호 안에서 알맞은 것끼리 짝지은 것은?
The new plan looks (A)[hope / hopeful], and the garden smells (B)[wonder / wonderful].
items.exp: look, smell 같은 감각동사 뒤에는 부사가 아니라 형용사가 와요. 명사 hope, wonder에 -ful을 붙인 hopeful, wonderful이 알맞아요.
items.passage:
hope + -ful → hopeful
wonder + -ful → wonderful

items.q: 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
items.exp: decide는 to부정사를 목적어로 취하므로 ④ decided use는 decided to use가 되어야 해요. ③ are는 plastic bags가 복수라 맞아요.
items.passage: I [① use] a reusable shopping bag. After I [② learned] that plastic bags [③ are] harmful to the environment, I [④ decided use] a reusable bag. I like it because it [⑤ reduces] waste and is durable.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
나는 내 텀블러가 친환경적이고 음료를 차갑게 유지해 주기 때문에 그것을 좋아한다.
choices: I like my tumbler because it is eco-friendly and keep drinks cold.
I like my tumbler because it is eco-friendly and keeping drinks cold.
I like my tumbler because of it is eco-friendly and keeps drinks cold.
I like my tumbler because it is eco-friendly and keeps drinks coldly.
I like my tumbler because it is eco-friendly and keeps drinks cold.
items.exp: because 뒤에는 절이 오고, is eco-friendly and keeps는 주어 it에 맞춘 병렬 구조예요. keeps drinks cold는 「keep+목적어+형용사」라 cold가 맞아요.
items.passage: I use a wooden toothbrush. After I learned that plastic is not good for the environment, I decided to change my toothbrush. I like my wooden toothbrush because it is eco-friendly and works well.
